recipes.name: Cheese and Bacon Jalapeno Rellenos
ingredients_raw: 0.5 (8 ounce) package PHILADELPHIA Cream Cheese, softened
1 cup KRAFT Mexican Style Shredded Four Cheese with a Touch of PHILADELPHIA
4 slices OSCAR MAYER Bacon, cooked, crumbled
18 jalapeno peppers, cut lengthwise in half, seeds and membranes removed

steps.text: Combine all ingredients except peppers; spoon into peppers.
Place, filled-sides up, on baking sheet.
Bake 10 min. or until cheese is melted.

raw_recipe.headline: Cheese and Bacon Jalapeno Rellenos
raw_recipe.description: Need a spicy, new starter? Our Cheese and Bacon Jalapeno Rellenos have an extra-creamy, extra exciting filling!

review.reviewBody: These are awesome. I have made them many times for parties, however, I boil my jalapenos for approximately 5 minutes prior to stuffing. It takes a little bite out of the pepper and makes it softer once baked. Always a crowd pleaser. Sure to disappear

I rate this appetizer a 5 with no hesitation! Followed the recipe to a "T" but followed the suggestion in the "Footnotes" below the recipe to add a tiny bit of ground red pepper to increase the "pop". I served these on an appetizer table in my living room right before serving Thanksgiving dinner and guests LOVED them! I did not boil the jalapenos ahead of time. Here in the Mid-South where I live, people expect some heat. The flavor of the filling was awesome!! Easy too! If some of your guests are vegetarians, you can save some cheese filling aside without the bacon, fill the peppers as usual, and bake along with the others. WILL make again!

Absolutely delicious! My guests loved these too. I added a slight bit more cream cheese. Also used fresh peppers from the garden. After baking for 10 mins, I put them on broil to get the tops golden brown. This is a hit!
Everyone loved them. I used red and yellow mini peppers which was perfect for the people for whom I was cooking. I will add more bacon next time.

I thought the mostly cream cheese recipes we boring. I saw this and it seemed interesting. Did the recipe just as written and it was excellent. I agree with others on boiling peppers. Takes away from the pepper taste and crunch so will eliminate that step next time.
Prepared as recipe directed but cooked in an air fryer vs. the oven. They were delicious. I will definitely make this recipe again.

SOOOO delicious! I was disappointed when I went to my cheese drawer and was out of cheddar cheese, which never happens! I wanted to make these really bad, so I used parmesan instead. I thought it worked great! I love how the bacon is pre-cooked then mixed in rather than wrapped around the jalapeno. I don't have to worry about if some of the bacon doesn't get cooked this way!

I have made these twice now and will probably make them again and again while I have hot peppers in my garden. Last night, a friend who was here for dinner, asked me if she could have the 3 that were left to take home with her. Following another reviewer's tip, I boiled the peppers for 5 minutes before stuffing them. They were delicious.

Just made these today and there were amazing! I used precooked bacon bits and that made prep even faster. Everyone loved them and I liked how easy they were to make. Next time I will wear gloves to seed the peppers as getting the jalapeño juice in open cuts hurts a lot.

I made these and they were a hit! My mother and aunt (both born and raised in Poland) have never eaten jalapeños and don't really do spicy (unlike me), so I did as another reviewer suggested and boiled them for a few minutes prior to stuffing. This definitely took away some of the kick, and because of that, they managed to polish off half of them by themselves! Love this recipe, though next time I might skip boiling so I can enjoy the intensity of the pepper.
I did enjoy them, but they aren’t the best that I’ve ever had. Very easy to make though. Would make again.

I’m not sure how small the jalapeños they used in this recipe were but I had to quadruple this recipe to fill 18. For the love of all things holy DO NOT boil your jalapeños first, just use those small bell peppers if you’re going to do that. If you scrape the membrane and seeds out, jalapeños are not that spicy folks. Also, it took 45 minutes of cooking for the jalapeños to get softened. Will definite make again as we all loved them and being in Texas we eat jalapeños all the time.
You can also use baby red and yellow peppers!
These are great. Had a bumper crop so made and froze these to enjoy all winter.

07.30.17 ~ Just picked our first round of jalapeños from the garden. I whipped up a small batch of the cheese mixture and stuffed it in 10 halves. Popped them in the toaster oven and 15 minutes later had a delicious side to go with our corn on the cob and fresh fruit. Super simple to make and a nice way to use up some jalapeños. I did wear gloves to handle the peppers while cleaning and stuffing them. So glad I did as two of them were particularly (spicy) hot. Like grab your glass of milk spicy!
Delicious, quick, and easy! I will definitely make these again.
Very good, really nice snack with low carbs
Great with pre-dinner drinks. Why not a margarita?
